turns.text: I'd like to practise a hard parent meeting. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. I'll send END MEETING on its own when I want to stop. I'm Owen's English teacher, and Meredith has just walked into my classroom.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Hi, thanks so much for coming. Coffee? It's terrible, but it's hot.
No, thank you. Who decided on the zero?
I want to start by saying Owen is one of my favorite students. This has been hard for me too.
Then you'll have no trouble answering me. Who decided, and did Owen get heard before it went in?
Here's what I have. The checker flagged 94%. I know those tools aren't perfect.

Not perfect. The company's own guide says that score should never be the sole basis for punishing a student, and your procedure says software alone doesn't establish anything. So is there anything else, or did a machine give my son a zero?
But the version history shows the file created at 11:31 PM, then 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58.

11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. What date, and have you turned that screen toward me yet? Before any of that, your own procedure says you speak to the student first and call me before a mark goes in, and you did neither.
You're being so fair about this. You're the kind of parent who makes this job worth doing.
Stop. You're dodging, Hale. Turn the screen around or tell me why Owen wasn't heard before that zero went in.
Can I tell you something? I've never had to run one of these meetings before. How am I doing? Be honest.
I'm not here to grade you. I'm here because my son has a zero he found out about on his phone. Show me that history or withdraw it.
There's also a quote in it. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' It isn't in Hamlet.
Students misquote Shakespeare all the time, Hale, that's a mistake, not proof of anything. Is that exact line in Owen's essay, and where?
And his October 15 outline went in a completely different direction.
Students change direction between an outline and an essay; that's called revising. You keep describing things and showing me nothing. Put the outline on the table.
Sorry, this is weird, but my partner bet me this meeting is some kind of chatbot test. Are you real? I know, I'll feel silly.
I'm sorry? Owen's essay.
Okay. What I want to offer is a supervised rewrite. Nothing goes on his record.
A rewrite for what? You haven't shown me one thing, and you haven't said whether the zero comes off.
What should I say to Owen so he takes it well? I'd really value your advice, mom to teacher.
You're asking me how to do your job? Show me the evidence and take the zero off, and I'll talk to my own son.
